hints: Find the first three terms of $(1-x)^6$: the constant, $x$, and $x^2$ terms.
Identify the three products with $(1-2x+5x^2)$ that produce $x^2$: $1 \times (x^2 \text{ term})$, $-2x \times (x \text{ term})$, and $5x^2 \times (\text{constant})$.
Compute $15(1) + (-6)(-2) + 1(5)$ to obtain the final coefficient.
walkthrough:
Determine the first three terms in the binomial expansion of $(1-x)^6$:
$$\text{Constant: } 1, \quad \text{Term in } x: \binom{6}{1}(-x) = -6x, \quad \text{Term in } x^2: \binom{6}{2}(-x)^2 = 15x^2$$

Identify all products that produce an $x^2$ term when $(1-2x+5x^2)$ is multiplied by $(1-x)^6$:
$$\text{From } 1 \times (15x^2) = 15x^2$$
$$\text{From } (-2x) \times (-6x) = 12x^2$$
$$\text{From } (5x^2) \times 1 = 5x^2$$

Sum the coefficients to find the total coefficient of $x^2$:
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^2 = 15 + 12 + 5 = 32$$
